locations.name: Oakhaven Swamp
locations.description: A fog-choked marsh of black water and dead cypress. Iron bells toll from a half-sunk Brotherhood watchtower at dusk, and the reeds hide wardens who never blink.

locations.name: River's End Docks
locations.description: A rope-tangled wharf city of stacked crates and salt smoke. Captain Vane's customs house squats on the eastern quay; smugglers swear the tide here runs backward on the new moon.

locations.name: Shrine of the Tideborn
locations.description: A drowned temple of black basalt, its altar slick with brine and older than the kingdom. Pilgrims leave coins in the shallow water and never see them again.

locations.name: Blackbriar Forest
locations.description: A thorn-choked wood where the canopy swallows daylight. Old Seraphine's wretched hut squats in a clearing of ash, and the briars grow back within the hour if cut.

lore.text: The Obsidian Brotherhood keeps its vigil in the black bogs of the Oakhaven Swamp. They are the drowned order of the Tideborn, monks who chose the dark water over the crown's law three generations ago. Their iron bells toll at dusk for every name the marsh claims, and the living keep a wide berth when the sound crosses the black water. Their wardens wear faceless cypress masks and carry flails wrapped in bell-rope. No one who has heard the bells in full peal has ever returned to speak of what they heard. The Brotherhood answers to no lord; they answer to the tide, and the tide does not forgive.

Vaelen once served the Tideborn as a bell-keeper at the drowned temple. He rang the vigil bells for seven years, standing in water that never warmed, until the night he broke the great bell with a stone and walked out of the swamp for the first time in a decade. The Brotherhood brands him a deserter and a defiler; the Shrine calls him the one who set the dead free. He carries a shard of the broken bell in his coat pocket and a debt he cannot repay. He speaks little, trusts less, and has been seen standing over the bodies of those who died within earshot of his bell.

Oakhaven Swamp was once the granary of the kingdom, a marsh of fat sedge and heron flocks. In the Drowning Year the river rose three nights in a row and took the granary, the causeways, and half the village. What remains is a fog-choked marsh of dead cypress where the water holds its breath. Travelers report that the drowned village is still visible below the surface at low tide, its window shutters open, its market stalls set for business. The local folk do not fish the black water, and they pay the toll to whoever rings the iron bells, though no one alive can name the order that owns them.

Captain Vane runs customs out of a customs house that leans on the eastern quay of River's End Docks. She is a former Tideborn quartermaster who traded her vigil for a manifest and a ledger, and she keeps both immaculately. Her rule is simple: every crate is inspected, every seal is broken and re-set, and every name on a manifest is a name she can collect on later. She trades in tideglass, dried sedge, and secrets, and she pays for all three in coin rather than favors. Smugglers who have worked the docks for a decade swear the tide runs backward on the new moon, and they never work the eastern quay on that night.

Old Seraphine lives in a wretched hut in a clearing of ash in the Blackbriar Forest, where the briars grow back within the hour if cut. She was a hedge-witch before the Drowning Year and a court apothecary after it, and she has kept both reputations ever since. She sells remedies for marsh-fever, bell-sickness, and the slow drowning that creeps up the legs of those who wade the black water. Her prices are steep and her haggling is worse, but she has never once sold a dose that did not work. Those who have been refused service by her tend not to come back, and those who have been refused twice tend not to come back at all.

The tideglass fragment in the player's pack is a shard of the great vigil bell that Vaelen broke with a stone on the night he walked out of the swamp. Tideglass rings true to the source bell even in silence; it warms when a Brotherhood warden is within earshot, and it sings in the dark if the owner is being lied to. The Shard is not magic in any sense the court would recognize. It is a debt, made glass. The Brotherhood would pay any coin for its return, and the Shrine would pay any coin for its keeping. The question is which of them the player believes, and whether the glass answers when it is held up to the ear.

On the night of the Drowning Festival the river is supposed to give back one thing it has taken. The tradition is old, older than the kingdom, and it is kept with a gravity that makes the living uneasy. The festival is a night of black lanterns, of coins cast into the black water, of the great bell rung once for every name in the drowned village's roll. This year the roll is shorter than it was last year, and the names that remain are not the names the village remembers. The Brotherhood has closed the watchtower to pilgrims, and the Shrine has stopped taking offerings. The water, the Tideborn say, is counting.

quests.title: The Swamp's Mystery
quests.description: Learn why the Brotherhood's iron bells toll for names the drowned village no longer remembers, and what the black water is counting toward.

quests.title: The Guild's Contract
quests.description: Deliver the sealed letter to Captain Vane at the River's End Docks. She will pay in coin, not favors, and she will inspect the seal before she opens it.

quests.title: Vaelen's Debt
quests.description: Vaelen owes the Shrine a life for the bell he broke. The debt is coming due, and the tideglass in your pack is the only proof it exists.

items.item_name: Chart of the River's End waterways

abilities.name: Tideglass Sense — feel the vigil bell's warmth through the fragment in your pack and know when a Brotherhood warden draws near
Wade the Black Water — cross the Oakhaven marsh without the slow drowning that creeps up the legs of those who wade it
Ring the Vigil — toll a name onto the drowned village's roll and hold a Brotherhood warden still for one long breath
